decisions.reason: Although it uses the firm's software and data-quality capabilities, address autocomplete is relatively generic and less tied to its distinctive regulated-energy knowledge base, so management would likely reallocate effort to more core platform modules.

An Austrian gas grid fee database is closely related to the firm's regulatory data and analytics strengths, and its in-house R&D should let it absorb country-specific rules and improve the offer commercially.

Peak load window determination fits the firm's existing calculation, compliance, and process know-how very well, making it a product the firm can readily refine and integrate into its broader SaaS platform.

The end-customer tariff database is close to the core business and, as a product line with several models, offers multiple learning opportunities that the firm can exploit through its databases, analytics, and modular platform strategy.

Custom web services are less scalable than standard SaaS, but they build on the firm's development and integration capabilities and can help it absorb customer needs that later feed standardized products.

A postal code lookup service is easy to build from existing capabilities but is peripheral and commoditized relative to the firm's specialized energy-market knowledge, so it is a plausible candidate to discontinue.
